This appeal coming on for admission this day, th e court  following:
 ORDER

This appeal by the claimants under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act is arising out of the award dated 11.07.2019 passed by MACT, Mandsaur in MACC No.323/2017 seeking enhancement of the amount of compensation awarded by the Tribunal.
2. The date of accident, negligence and the issue of liability are not in dispute and the findings recorded by the Tribunal in this regard are also not in question.

As per the findings of the Tribunal,
for the death of Prakashchandra Patidar, the Tribunal has awarded a total compensation of Rs.6,04,500/- along with interest.

The break up of the compensation amount is as under:
L o s s o f d e p e n d e n c y - R s . 5 , 4 4 , 5 0 0 / - ( i . e . R s . 5 0 0 0 1 0 % f u t u r e prospects=5500x12=Rs.66000-1/4personal expenses=49500x11(multiplier)) Funeral expenses -Rs.15,000/-

Loss of consortium -Rs.40,000/-
 Loss of estate -Rs.15,000/-
 --------------------

2 3.
Learned counsel for the appellants submits that the Tribunal has committed an error in awarding just and proper amount of compensation in the case as the amount awarded is on the lower side.
The Tribunal has committed an error in assessing the income of the deceased at Rs.5000/- per month.
The deceased was working in oil mill and was earning Rs.15,000/- per month.

The compensation given under the head of loss of consortium is also on the lower side in the light of the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Nanu Ram & others.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Nanu Ram & others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The compensation awarded under other conventional heads is also on the lower side,
hence prays for just and proper amount of compensation in the case.
4.

On the other hand, learned counsel for the Insurance Company has argued in support of the impugned award and contended that the Claims Tribunal has rightly awarded the compensation amount in the case which does not call for any interference by this Court.
5. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going the record, I find substance in the arguments advanced by the counsel for the appellants.
As per the evidence of wife of the deceased, the deceased was working in Oil Mill and was earning Rs.15000/- per month.
The accident was of the year 2016.

Considering the evidence came on record, in the considered opinion of this Court, the Tribunal has committed an error in assessing the income of the deceased at Rs.5000/- per month which is on the very lower side and deserves to be enhanced to Rs.6500/- per month.
The Apex Court in the case of Nanu Ram (supra) has interpreted the term "consortium" to be a compendious term which encompasses spousal consortium, parental consortium as well as filial consortium.
The right to consortium would include the company, care, help comfort, guidance, solace and affection of the deceased which is a loss to the whole family.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the number of dependents of the deceased's family and the fact that he was the only bread winner of his family, the compensation amount deserves to be enhanced as under:
Loss of dependency -Rs.6500 10% future prospects=7150x12=85800 - 1/4 personal expenses=64350x11(multiplier)=7,07,850/-
 Loss of consortium -Rs.2,20,000/- (i.e. Rs.4  Funeral expenses -Rs.16,500/-
 Loss of estate -Rs.16,500/-
 -------------------
 TOTAL Rs.9,60,850/-
 ============
6.
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the case is Rs.9,60,850/ as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs.6,04,500/-.

Accordingly, the appellants are entitled to an additional sum of Rs.3,56,350/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.
7. Accordingly, the appeal is partly allowed by enhancing the amount by a sum of Rs.3,56,350/-.
The enhanced amount shall bear interest at the same rate as awarded by the Tribunal.
The other findings recorded by the Tribunal shall remain intact.

(HIRDESH) JUDGE hk/
